name: What are the common types of fire extinguisher residue?

mainEntity.name: What are the common types of fire extinguisher residue?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common types of fire extinguisher residue come from dry chemical and wet chemical extinguishers. Dry chemical extinguishers, frequently found in homes and businesses, leave behind a fine, powdery substance, typically monoammonium phosphate or sodium bicarbonate. This powder can be corrosive to metals and electronics. Wet chemical extinguishers, used for kitchen fires, leave a soapy, foamy residue that is generally easier to clean but can still be slippery and require thorough removal. CO2 extinguishers leave no residue, while water-based ones leave water damage.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common residues include dry chemical powder (corrosive to metals/electronics) and wet chemical foam (soapy). CO2 leaves no residue, and water extinguishers cause water damage.
